topics.label: Introduction to cancer hallmarks and mutation progression
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecture framework, learning outcomes, and the multi-step model of cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Deregulated growth signaling pathways in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenic mutations in cell-surface receptors and downstream intracellular cascades drive autonomous cell proliferation and survival.

topics.label: Blocks in terminal cell differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how failure of precursor cells to terminally differentiate sustains proliferative capacity in both hematopoietic and epithelial malignancies.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details how cancer cells resist programmed cell death through the disruption of p53 signaling and the imbalance of mitochondrial apoptotic regulators.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, senescence, and stress-response mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how telomere shortening, senescence, and p53-mediated stress responses limit cellular lifespan and how tumor cells overcome these controls to achieve immortalization.

topics.label: Altered cellular metabolism and metabolic rewiring in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address how oncogenic changes rewire cellular metabolic pathways, including aerobic glycolysis and oncometabolite production, to support tumor growth.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the angiogenic switch and the mechanisms by which expanding tumors stimulate new blood vessel formation to overcome hypoxia and nutrient deprivation.

topics.label: Mechanisms, dissemination, and genomics of cancer metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics investigate the multi-step metastatic cascade, patterns of systemic dissemination, the seed and soil hypothesis, and the genomic characteristics of secondary tumors.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: This closing subtopic summarises the core takeaways of the lecture, highlights recent literature on cancer hallmarks, and provides concluding remarks.
